messages.subject: can you match with "post-treatment" variables?
messages.body_plain:
Hey all-

I'm diving into the ANES panel data, and I find myself wanting to
match with variables that were collected in a wave that was collected
AFTER the treatment variable was collected.

Thoughts? Is this contingent on whether you can argue that the
treatment (theoretically) had no effect on the post-treatment
covariate?

Best,

-c

-- 
Casey A. Klofstad
University of Miami
Department of Political Science
Coral Gables, FL

messages.body_plain:
In all likelihood, that wouldn't be a good idea
unless the variables measured post-treatment had the same values
pre-treatment.  E.g., race, sex, etc.



Gary

messages.subject: Re: MatchIt stops responding
messages.body_plain:
Minh,

The issue seems to be that you're conducting full matching with the
exact same number of treated and control units with a restriction of
max.controls=1.  This appears problematic when there are multiple
control units that are identical on all covariates (subclassification
doesn't work when no subclasses can be generated with exactly 1
treated and 1 control unit) .  See the output for:

mse.out<-matchit(rankcfa~tcap08 + READ08 + SCI08,
                 data=mse, method="exact")

Changing max.controls to 2 in your call to matchit() runs for me:

mse.out<-matchit(rankcfa~tcap08 + READ08 + SCI08,
                 data=mse, method="full", max.controls=2)

Since you don't really appear to be interested in full matching,
another way to achieve this seems to be:

mse.out<-matchit(rankcfa~tcap08 + READ08 + SCI08,
                 data=mse, method="optimal", ratio=1)

I hope that helps, and I'd suggest looking into the details of
optmatch if you're interested.

Dan

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Peter,
I figured it out--
dim(all) returned 219 columns, but I only had 217 columns of data.  Must
have been that R was trying to read some of the blank columns at the end,
and thus returning the undefined column error because they had no data.  I
therefore used the command you suggested allr<-all[1:1460,1:217] with a
dimension of two fewer columns, which truncated the bad columns at the end.


Toby

messages.subject: can a variable be used as a co-variate and a dependent variable?
messages.subject_clean: can a variable be used as a co-variate and a dependent variable?
messages.body_plain:
Hey all-

In a paper I'm reviewing one of the covariates used in a 1-to-1
matching procedure ends up also being used as the dependent variable
in the final analysis. From a theoretical point of view this seems
odd, since the variable is being treated as both a pre- and
post-treatment variable. But, is there any empirical reason to be
worried about this?

Thanks much,

-c

--
Casey A. Klofstad
University of Miami
Department of Political Science
Coral Gables, FL

messages.subject_clean: can a variable be used as a co-variate and a dependent variable?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Casey,
Matching on the outcome is certainly problematic....imagine if you got perfect balance (which you would hope to do), then that would also imply a 0 treatment effect!

What wouldn't be problematic (and in fact would be good) is if they were actually matching on a pre-treatment measure of the outcome.  E.g., in education studies there is often pre-treatment test scores available, where those same tests form the outcome value as well (but then measured post-treatment).   This kind of matching on the outcome variables (but measured before the treatment) can be very effective.

Thanks
Liz

damned if you don't" applies
